literal: Equity called one thing is good indeed, by the divisions having taken the proper side to behave if achieved.
translation: That one quality called equity is truly good, provided one can conduct oneself justly toward every division of people.
modern: பகைவர், அயலார், நண்பர் என அனைவரிடமும் அவரவர்க்கு உரிய நீதியோடு நடுவுநிலைமை தவறாமல் நடந்துகொள்ள முடிந்தால், தகுதி என்று சொல்லப்படும் அந்த ஒரு குணமே மிகவும் நல்லதாகும்.
explanation: The couplet emphasizes the supreme value of impartiality, referred to here as 'takuti' (equity or fitness). It states that this single quality is inherently good. The condition for this goodness is expressed in the second line: one must manage to behave ('oḻuka peṟiṉ') by taking the proper side ('pāṟpaṭṭu') according to the different divisions of people ('pakutiyāl'). In this context, 'pakuti' refers to the natural divisions of people in one's life, such as friends, enemies, and strangers, and true equity means treating each group with the same unwavering justice.
